paper.title: No-Regret Online Autobidding Algorithms in First-price Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated first-price auctions with ROI constraint, known competing bid distribution F
unmapped: Bidding in repeated first-price auctions: bid b in [0,1], win if b >= competing bid d_t ~ F i.i.d., pay b on win
Value v_t i.i.d. from unknown H observed before bidding (acts as context)
ROI (return-on-investment) constraint: total payment <= total value obtained, in expectation; ROI violation also bounded
Competing bid distribution F is known to the learner
Benchmark: optimal (possibly randomized) bidding strategy in hindsight knowing F and the value sequence
settings.definition_quote: In this subsection, we describe a no-regret online bidding algorithm (see \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F}) when the competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ is known to the bidder, while the value distribution $\valDist$ still remains unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated first-price auctions with ROI constraint, full feedback
unmapped: Bidding in repeated first-price auctions: bid b in [0,1], win if b >= competing bid d_t ~ F i.i.d. (unknown), pay b on win
Value v_t i.i.d. from unknown H observed before bidding (acts as context)
ROI constraint: total payment <= total value obtained, in expectation; ROI violation also bounded
Benchmark: optimal (possibly randomized) bidding strategy in hindsight knowing F and the value sequence
settings.definition_quote: \textbf{Full feedback:} At the end of round $t$, the bidder observes the competing bid $d_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated first-price auctions with ROI constraint, bandit (one-bit) feedback
unmapped: Bidding in repeated first-price auctions: bid b in [0,1], win if b >= competing bid d_t ~ F i.i.d. (unknown), pay b on win
Only the win/lose bit is observed after each round (value v_t is observed beforehand, so realized reward and payment are known)
Value v_t i.i.d. from unknown H observed before bidding (acts as context)
ROI constraint: total payment <= total value obtained, in expectation; ROI violation also bounded
Benchmark: optimal (possibly randomized) bidding strategy in hindsight knowing F and the value sequence
settings.definition_quote: \textbf{Bandit feedback:} At the end of round $t$, the bidder only receives a binary signal $\win_t\in\{0, 1\}$ indicating whether she won the item or not, i.e., $\win_t = \indicator{\competingbid_t \le \bid_t}$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1: No-regret bidding algorithm for known F (dual mirror descent on concavified F_conv)
Algorithm 2: No-regret bidding algorithm with full feedback (stage-based restarts with optimistic empirical CDF)
Algorithm 3: No-regret bidding algorithm with bandit feedback (explore grid bids, then conservative Algorithm 1)

source.label: prop:performance algo known F
source.quote: For any unknown value distribution $\valDist$, the expected regret of \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F} under any competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ is bounded by $\TotalRegret(\text{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) = O(\sqrt{T})$, and the expected ROI violation is bounded by ... \le 2\log T \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected rewards v_t F(b_t) against optimal randomized strategy in hindsight satisfying the ROI constraint; mapped to pseudo_regret with best_feasible_policy comparator.

conditions: quantity is the expected ROI violation (total payment minus total value)

source.label: thm:randomized_algorithm_full_feedback
source.quote: For any unknown competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ and unknown value distribution $\valDist$, under the setting with full feedback, the expected regret of \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy}  is bounded by $\TotalRegret(\mathrm{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) = \widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$, and the expected ROI violation is bounded by ... $= \widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Comparator is optimal randomized strategy in hindsight (knowing F and V^T) under the ROI constraint.

conditions: quantity is the expected ROI violation

tuning: M = Theta(sqrt(T)) rounds per grid point

source.label: thm:bandit_feedback-regret_ros
source.quote: For any unknown competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ and unknown value distribution $\valDist$, under the bandit feedback, the expected regret of \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_with_bandit_feedback} with $M = \Theta(\sqrt{T}), K = \Theta(T^{\sfrac{1}{4}})$ is bounded by ... $= \widetilde O(T^{\sfrac{3}{4}})$, and the expected ROI violation is bounded by ... $= \widetilde O(T^{\sfrac{3}{4}})$.

results.notes: Paper's K is the number of grid intervals (algorithm parameter), not number of arms. Bandit feedback = win bit only; mapped to bandit since value is observed so realized reward is known.
